subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff — SandboxAI workload profile and sizing inputs
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <ops@sandboxai.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff — Redwood x SandboxAI

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — excited about the potential to run your inference pipeline on a Dedicated pool. To move the sizing and contract discussion forward I need a short workload profile we can use to model throughput and cost. Could you send the items below by end of week? If easier, feel free to drop a sample file (CSV/JSON) and I can ingest it.

Requested workload inputs (short answers are fine):
- Average QPS and observed peak QPS (local timezone) over a typical week.
- Typical session length / average number of turns per user (if multi-turn).
- Input prompt size (tokens) and average model response size (tokens).
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs. non-streaming.
- SLA expectations (p95 latency target, availability).
- Estimated retention / KV cache behavior (do you re-use context prefixes?).
- Any special model variants (mix of medium prompts vs. long generation) or custom weights.

If you already have a sample of production traffic, please attach it (anonymized is fine). I attached a small template CSV to make copy/paste easy.

Once I have this we’ll loop in Karthik and Aditya for a quick sizing sketch (GPU type, reserved capacity, and burst policy).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions (Pre-Sales)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: workload_template.csv (csv, 2KB)]

From: Jordan Price <ops@sandboxai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff — Redwood x SandboxAI

Hi Laura,

Thanks — attached is a sanitized sample of last week's traffic and a short notes file. Quick answers inline below and files attached: traffic_samples.csv, sample_prompts.txt.

- Average QPS: 12 requests/sec. Peak QPS: 210 requests/sec (typically 11:30–12:30 PT weekdays).
- Session length: 1.8 turns average; heavy users can hit 8–12 turns.
- Prompt sizes: median 60 tokens; 90th percentile 420 tokens.
- Response size: median 120 tokens; 90th percentile 1600 tokens for long-form generation (rare ~4%).
- Streaming: ~28% of requests use streaming (progressive generation for UI).
- SLA: Looking for p95 < 250ms for short prompts, p95 < 2s for long-form; availability target 99.9%.
- Cache/prefix reuse: We reuse a stable 64-token system prompt for ~60% of requests. No persistent KV between sessions.
- Models: Currently using an open LLM family (opt-cc-like) with a custom head; willing to evaluate quantized 4-bit variants.

Notes file includes a small breakdown by endpoint (chat vs. generate) and two example long prompts that drive the heavy token cases.

Let me know if you need anything else — happy to jump on a quick call with your sizing team.

—Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Platform
Sandbox AI, Inc.
[Attachment: traffic_samples.csv (csv, 42KB)]
[Attachment: sample_prompts.txt (txt, 3KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity kickoff — Redwood x SandboxAI (initial sizing)

Laura — thanks for the context and the sample. Initial sizing notes below; this is an engineering-first sketch that we should refine after a short test run.

Summary estimate (conservative):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs (NVIDIA A10G / 24GB perf class). Assumes mixed-precision 4-bit quantized model to fit long sequences efficiently.
- Concurrency assumptions: target 16 concurrent short-chat sessions per GPU at median prompt length (60 in / 120 out tokens). For long-form jobs, plume-style batching yields ~2 long jobs concurrently per GPU when response tokens > 1k.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~160–180 QPS sustained on the reserved pool for mixed profile when autoscale not active. This covers most weekdays; short peak windows (210 QPS) require burst capacity.
- Burst policy: allow burst to cloud burst tier of 4 additional GPUs (pay-as-you-go) to cover +25% headroom. Recommend an autoscale trigger at 85% GPU utilization observed over 3 minutes.
- Latency: with prefix cache (64-token system prompt cached) we can meet p95 < 250ms for short prompts under 75% utilization. Long-form p95 ~1–2s depending on sampling settings; streaming path will add slight overhead but keeps perceived latency low.
- Caching: enable prefix caching and a 10-minute LRU for repeated contexts; this should cut token decode cost ~15% for Sandbox's profile.
- Ops playbook: pre-warm 2 reserved GPUs before daily peak window (11:15 PT), schedule an incremental scale at 60% utilization to avoid hitting 85% threshold suddenly. Include an emergency fallback to a smaller model variant when token queue grows.

Open questions / risks:
1) Model size and attention horizon — we need exact model parameter count and tokenizer to validate memory footprint for 1.6k response generation. If model > 20B or has large KV, GPU count may increase.
2) Multi-turn KV reuse — confirm if any sessions exceed 12 turns persistently; if so we should budget more RAM for KV caches.
3) Long-run streaming scale test — recommend a 24h soak test at 110% of observed peak to validate autoscale and latency SLO.

Deliverables: I attached a quick calc (initial_sizing_estimate.pdf) and a one-page ops checklist. If Sandbox can run a 2-hour load test using our test plan we can convert this estimate into a firm committed capacity proposal and pricing.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
